source: flip each bit of up to 16 Apple-emitted instances per (opcode,length) and read the register Apple's decoder (agxforge.g17.model.decode) reports; a bit enters a map only when every instance agrees on one power-of-two step and the instruction keeps its opcode and length
units: [weight, byte, bit, invert]; weight is log2 of the step in 16-bit register halves (R n = 2n, H = 2n+1). A 32-bit operand has no H bit, so its lowest weight is 1
finding: The slot layout depends on ENCODED LENGTH. Neither isa/g17-contract.jsonl (pre-repair) nor isa/g17-authoring.jsonl (the 3c6ff37c repair) is right at every length of any form in which the length changes the layout. At the longest length the pre-repair map is exact for 21 forms, where the repair adds a weight-9 bit that at that length does not move the register (it is a short-length bit). For 14 forms both maps omit the H bit and the repair appends it as the HIGHEST weight; it is the LOWEST (every other weight moves up one). 437 and 17757 are the two the repair gets right at the longest length.
